sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and counter
sections.what: Brings in the test tools and sets a running counter that makes each new user unique within one test run.
sections.why: The counter prevents two users created in the same moment from sharing an email.

sections.name: newUser
sections.title: Creating a fresh test user
sections.what: Builds a unique user, registers them through the sign-up API with the age confirmation, and returns their details.
sections.why: Gives each test an isolated account so tests do not share data.
sections.watch_out: The fake client address is derived from counters and time, so it can still collide under heavy load.

sections.name: signInUi
sections.title: Signing in through the login form
sections.what: Opens the login page, fills in the email and password, submits, and waits until the browser leaves the login address.
sections.why: Tests sign-in the way a real user does, rather than setting a session directly.
sections.watch_out: The twenty-second wait is needed because password hashing is slow, so shortening it will cause flaky runs.

summary: Test helpers that create a new user through the sign-up API and sign that user into the browser through the login form.
purpose: Gives every browser test a fresh, separate account without repeating the sign-up steps.
why: Each test needs its own user so tests do not interfere with one another.
how: The user creation helper builds a unique email and password from the current time, the process number and a counter. It posts to the registration endpoint with the age confirmation and a fake client address that varies per user. It expects a created response and returns the user. The sign-in helper goes to the login page, fills in the email and password, clicks sign in, and waits for the page to leave the login address, allowing up to twenty seconds for slow password hashing.
inputs: A request context for the user creation helper, or a browser page and user details for sign-in, plus a name for new accounts.
outputs: The new user's email, password and name, or a finished sign-in on the page.
risks: The fake client address is built from a counter and time, so heavy parallel runs could still collide with sign-up rate limits.
debug: If sign-up fails, check the status code and the rate limit. If sign-in times out, check whether the login form labels match.
